claims.summary: After writing a fitting array of 32-bit values at the supplied address, the export returns their 32-bit wrapping sum.
claims.statement:
∀ (p : BitVec 32) (xs : List (BitVec 32)),
  p.toNat + 4 * xs.length ≤ 65536 →
    FVA.Wasm.Exec.ReturnsAfterWrite Examples.Mem.Lifted.module p.toNat (FVA.Wasm.Exec.le32s xs) "array_sum"
      [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 p, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 xs.length)] [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 xs.sum]
claims.reason: The bound forces the list length to be at most 16,384, so its length fits the 32-bit argument; the statement returns the wrapping sum for every fitting array.
claims.name: Examples.Mem.arraySum
claims.intent:
`array_sum(p, n)`: the sum, wrapped to 32 bits, of the `n` unsigned 32-bit words `xs` that
the caller wrote at address `p`, for every array inside the module's 64 KiB memory (so
`n ≤ 16384`: the length argument never wraps).
details: Covers every 32-bit pointer bit pattern and every finite list of 32-bit elements.
The pointer is converted to an unsigned natural byte address; the list length is passed as a 32-bit value.

The caller writes each element as four little-endian bytes. The bound ensures the write ends within the first 65,536 bytes, but does not itself guarantee the module’s memory is large enough; ReturnsAfterWrite additionally requires suitable fresh instances under every host behavior.

The returned list sum uses 32-bit bit-vector addition, so it wraps modulo 2 to the 32nd power. ReturnsAfterWrite guarantees the export is callable, terminates without trapping, and returns exactly that value in every qualifying fresh instance.
caveats: Claim 1 is conditional on the address-and-length fit bound and says nothing about memory contents outside the written array.

claims.summary: The classification export applies one of five specified 32-bit operations according to the first argument’s unsigned value, and returns zero for all other values.
claims.statement:
∀ (x y : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Mem.Lifted.module "classify" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 y]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32
        (match x.toNat with
        | 0 => y + 7
        | 1 => y <<< 3
        | 2 => y ^^^ 85#32
        | 3 => y * 100
        | 4 => y - 9
        | x => 0)]
claims.reason: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the statement applies the specified wrapped operation for cases 0–4 and returns zero otherwise.
claims.name: Examples.Mem.classify
claims.intent:
`classify(x, y)` on unsigned 32-bit ints, by the case `x`: `y + 7`, `y << 3`, `y xor 0x55`,
`100 y`, `y − 9` for `x` = 0 … 4 (wrapped to 32 bits), else 0.
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit bit patterns.
The first argument is matched using its unsigned natural value; the second is manipulated as a 32-bit bit vector, without signed interpretation.
Addition, left shift, multiplication, and subtraction wrap at 32 bits; the shift is a 32-bit left shift, and XOR is bitwise.
Returns guarantees the module is instantiable and that every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified 32-bit result.
caveats: The cases inspect the unsigned natural value of the first argument, not a signed interpretation.
Values outside the five listed cases return zero, even if their signed interpretation would be small or negative.

claims.summary: The export returns the 32-bit wrapping sum of two scaled-and-offset values, one computed from the input and one from the input incremented with wraparound.
claims.reason: The statement computes the same two scaled-and-offset terms, including 32-bit wraparound of the increment and result, for every input.
claims.name: Examples.Mem.callScale
claims.intent: `call_scale(x)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `(3x + 1) + (3(x + 1) + 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: All arithmetic is 32-bit bit-vector arithmetic and wraps modulo 2 to the 32nd power; no value is read as signed.
Returns guarantees the module is instantiable and that every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified result.
caveats: The expression specifies arithmetic solely in 32-bit bit-vector terms; it does not assert that the compiled function follows a source-language signed-integer interpretation.
